source.title: Kernel interpolation generalizes poorly
source.authors: Yi-Cheng Li; Haobo Zhang; Qian Lin

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves lower bounds on generalization error for kernel interpolation and for wide neural networks through an NTK approximation, using a different setting and theoretical measure from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies noisy regression on a sphere, not fitting random labels and generalizing on natural classification labels. It does not test the specific conditions in V1–V8. Cited prior-work results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves sample-size lower bounds for noisy regression with kernel interpolation and sufficiently wide neural networks. These results do not compare natural and random labels (V1), or establish how test error changes with width beyond interpolation (V2). It tests none of V3–V8 either.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors interpret their lower bounds as poor generalization for kernel interpolation and the specified wide networks, and suggest another perspective is needed to explain benign overfitting. The precise result restricts convergence rates; as Remark 3.2 states, it does not establish inconsistency.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives theoretical results for kernel interpolation and gradient-flow-trained two-layer ReLU networks on noisy sphere regression; it does not reproduce the classification experiments or interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The results rely on the stated eigenvalue decay, embedding-index, kernel continuity, and non-vanishing-noise assumptions; the neural-network corollary also uses sufficiently large width and symmetric initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3.1 bounds kernel interpolation's conditional expected squared L2 regression error below by cσ²n^−ε for every ε > 0, with high probability for sufficiently large n.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In fixed dimensions, under polynomial eigenvalue decay, embedding index 1/β, Hölder continuity, and non-vanishing noise, kernel interpolation's expected regression error cannot decay at any positive polynomial rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Corollary 4.2 extends the lower bound to the limiting regression error of sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks with symmetric initialization, trained by gradient flow on uniformly distributed sphere inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the specified noisy sphere-regression assumptions, sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks trained to interpolation have a limiting expected regression-error lower bound of cσ²n^−ε.

record.problems: The results are asymptotic theoretical lower bounds under assumptions, not empirical measurements. The authors state that Theorem 3.1 does not imply inconsistency because the sufficiently large sample size depends on ε and δ. The neural-network result applies through an NTK approximation and is limited to the specified sphere regression setting.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results were left out. Results from cited prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label versus random-label classification accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Changes in test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The authors' broad discussion of benign overfitting does not make these results a test of V1 or V2. A lower bound as sample size grows establishes neither failure of above-chance classification nor worsening test error as width grows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit fixed random labels and compare held-out natural-label accuracy with random-label accuracy.
No width sweep around the interpolation threshold or test-error comparison across widths.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.

rows.operation_detail: Theorem lower-bounds conditional expected squared L2 generalization error for kernel interpolation under the stated assumptions.

conditions.value: n i.i.d. samples; non-vanishing conditional noise
fixed-dimensional compact input space under the paper's assumptions

rows.measure: Conditional expected squared L2 error E[||fˆinter − fρ*||²L2 | X]
rows.value: At least cσ² n^−ε with probability at least 1 − δ, for any ε > 0 and sufficiently large n.
rows.uncertainty: High-probability statement: at least 1 − δ; c > 0 is an absolute constant.
rows.note: The theorem is a lower bound, not an empirical estimate; the paper notes it does not imply inconsistency because the required n depends on ε and δ.
rows.check: The theorem and reported bound are correctly extracted, but 'observed' cannot describe evidence for any listed version. This is a theoretical lower bound on regression error, not a measurement of a listed effect.

rows.uncertainty: High-probability statement: at least 1 − δ; c > 0 is a constant.
